prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology and active peptide forms of glucagon-like peptide-1 that made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: I keep B019 as my single prize part with Holst, Drucker and Mojsov, and my configuration has not changed since round 1. Round 1 showed that the six of us agree on the science and on maturity, so the open questions are about credit. On science, the arc is complete. Holst established gut incretin physiology and GLP-1 secretion. Drucker established proglucagon-derived peptide biology and the gut and islet actions. Mojsov identified and synthesised the truncated active peptide. Large independent randomized trials then confirmed durable benefit in type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal signals emerging. The evidence is replicated and the recognition is timely. I also accept the chair's observation that agreement on a configuration is not the same as agreement that the credit is settled. My position rests on the scientific and clinical case. It does not rest on the opening vote count.
statement.case_against: The weak point is the third place. I cannot settle the priority question between Mojsov and the Habener group from the material I am allowed to read. What I recall is that the active truncated form, GLP-1(7-36), was characterised and shown to be insulinotropic in the mid-1980s by more than one laboratory, and that Mojsov's contribution included its identification and synthesis. I treat that as recollection, not documentation, and I would not want the prize to depend on it. Knudsen's exclusion is a real cost, because there is no second prize part in which to honour drug development within the three-person cap. B002 has the cleaner two-person credit and the stronger conceptual originality. If the documentary record shows that Mojsov's priority is not defensible, and I do not think Knudsen should replace her without examination, I would move to B002 and not rebuild B019 around a weak third name. B002's own caveat is that PERK and ATF6 work in mammalian cells could blur a clean Walter and Mori credit, and its disease translation is still early.

responses.point: The chair asks whether B002 can wait without loss while the B019 attribution is checked, and whether any member supports deferring B019 on that basis.
responses.response: I do not support deferring B019 for that reason. B002 can wait. Its mechanism is mature, its two-person credit does not change with time, and no event this year weakens it. B019 is different: the attribution question can be resolved by checking the primary papers, and it concerns one of three names. It does not call the discovery into doubt. Deferring would also not fix the Knudsen problem. So I treat sequencing as a reason to check Mojsov's priority before the vote and not as a reason to shelve B019. If the check fails, my first fallback is B002 and not an incretin trio that includes Knudsen and Holst or Drucker alone. I accept your point that I placed B002 first in the opening. I moved because of the reasons I gave, not because of the count.

responses.point: Linnarsson would openly weigh Knudsen for the third place if the Habener dispute proved unresolvable, and says contested attribution might make B002 or a different B019 configuration more robust.
responses.response: I understand the logic but I would take it in two steps. If Mojsov's priority is unresolved but not refuted, I would keep her. The citation is built on identification of the active form, and Knudsen's work is optimisation of a drug on a principle already established. Substituting Knudsen would change the citation from discovery to development, and the same fairness objection would then fall on Mojsov, Habener and others. If Mojsov's priority is refuted, I would choose B002 over a Knudsen substitution, because a mixed discovery-and-development trio would no longer match the citation I am defending. I can accept the Knudsen exclusion only if it is recorded openly as a cost.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius wants the Mojsov credit paragraph checked against primary publications before the final vote and would not make the prize depend on her if the evidence is weaker than recalled, while also asking whether the UPR should displace GLP-1 if attribution proves unsafe.
responses.response: I agree with checking the primary record, and I make the same commitment: if the dated evidence shows Mojsov's role is weaker than we remember, I move to B002. I would set the threshold clearly. A shared or disputed priority that the citation can describe accurately is not enough to move me, because the citation does not say Mojsov was first. A finding that the active-form identification or synthesis should be credited mainly to someone outside the supplied names, with no defensible role for Mojsov, would move me. I therefore keep B019 now, and I would not describe it as safe if the record is ambiguous.

responses.point: Perlmann opposes any B019 split and treats Knudsen's contribution as recognised through the therapeutic route, while keeping B008 as an alternative.
responses.response: In round 1 I agreed on the trio but said the therapeutic-route argument fails if no such route exists in the configuration. I stay with that. For citation wording, I would use 'physiology and active peptide forms' and not name any drug, so the text does not imply that the drugs were unimportant. I also record in the committee's reasoning that Knudsen's medicinal chemistry is excluded by the three-person cap. On your B008 alternative, I regard CAR-T as clinically strong but the Eshhar gap is a credit hole of the same size as B004, so I keep B002 and B004 as my alternatives. B002 is the stronger fallback on credit, and B004 is the stronger one on science and breadth.

responses.point: Sandberg describes the Mojsov-Habener issue as choosing among well-documented contributors, not doubt about the discovery, and treats the UPR as the strongest next candidate.
responses.response: I partly agree. The discovery is not in doubt, but I would not call the contributors 'well documented' in this committee's file: the Habener group is outside the supplied credit, and none of us can verify dates. That is why I do not want the vote to treat attribution as already resolved. My ordering of fallbacks follows the credit risk. B002 comes first because its credit is clean and its mechanism is confirmed across systems. B004 comes second because its six-way credit problem is serious, but the science of channelrhodopsin discovery and neuronal deployment is exceptional.

uncertainties: Primary-source dates for who first showed the insulinotropic activity of GLP-1(7-36) and who first synthesised it; my account is recollection only, and the Habener group is not on the supplied credit.
Whether Knudsen's exclusion can be recorded in the committee reasoning in a way that does not read as favouring academic discovery over industrial development.
Whether mammalian PERK and ATF6 work weakens the Walter and Mori credit for B002 enough to change my fallback ordering.
Whether long-term safety and durability of weight loss with incretin therapy will change the maturity assessment.
statement.conflict_note: No documented tie to any credited name on B019, B002 or B004, and I request no recusal. For transparency I note a 2009 co-authored paper with Thomas Perlmann on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons and a 2019 synthesis with Sten Grillner; neither concerns a shortlisted credited name. Round 1 raised no new conflict.
